procedure.method: I visually inspected the nine exact pinned poster PNGs through tools.view_image with detail='original', forwarding each returned image as image content. The inspection order was M1 native, usage720, thumbnail320; M2 native, usage720, thumbnail320; M3 native, usage720, thumbnail320. All nine image outputs were seen before any transcription judgment, image score or diversity score. SHA-256, byte sizes and actual PNG IHDR dimensions were checked against the pins. I read the three pinned native-evidence manifests without following their embedded source, input or final paths. No source assets or protected-layout measurement manifests were supplied (both packet arrays are empty), so those procedure lists are empty. Copy comparisons use the predeclared nfc-ws-optical-v1 rule; first visual reads, soft wrapping and normalized comparisons are separate. No ambiguity-triggered revisits were needed. I worked independently in this fresh task, without spawning, peer reviews, author explanations or an invented session/thread identity.

evidence.observation: This member is an opaque portrait 2:3 poster with all 24 protected copy entries and substantial urban nonglyph content. Its open rendering style was judged only against the literal client conditions.

evidence.location: right column from upper title to venue, agenda, audience and red registration URLs
evidence.observation: The large Korean and English title leads into the event identification and venue. Aligned time rows and horizontal dividers distinguish the programme, audience, registration and contact blocks; red URLs make the action easy to locate.

evidence.location: green canopy, orange storefront and navy text on cream
evidence.observation: Sunlit greenery and a warm doorway give the event an inviting energy. The restrained, high-contrast information column sustains an institutional tone appropriate to a practical forum.

evidence.location: left approximately half of poster, tree-lined sidewalk and pale blue silhouettes beside the text column
evidence.observation: The substantial painted streetscape establishes urban everyday life. Its adjoining pale building and tree outlines simplify the same kind of scene, but no visible collection, comparison, encoding or arrangement connects those observations to data; the specific forum topic is carried mainly by the words.

evidence.location: illustrated or photographic scene and all text blocks
evidence.observation: No added factual map labels, scales or measurements are visible. The depicted setting is unlabeled; the numeric information is the supplied event date, programme and capacity. No added logo or sponsor copy appears.

issues: The literal requirement to show the relationship between observing the city and data is not met clearly enough by a pleasant streetscape and pale urban outlines. The large visual establishes urban context, but its nonglyph content does not show an observable data relationship.

ratio.observation: 1024 × 3 = 1536 × 2 = 3072. Native portrait ratio is mathematically exact 2:3; no rescaling or rounding exception was used.

evidence.observation: The large scene has recognizable urban forms and actions; it is not glyph-only output, type alone, texture or token ornament.

content_form.location: left approximately half of poster, tree-lined sidewalk and pale blue silhouettes beside the text column
content_form.observation: The substantial painted streetscape establishes urban everyday life. Its adjoining pale building and tree outlines simplify the same kind of scene, but no visible collection, comparison, encoding or arrangement connects those observations to data; the specific forum topic is carried mainly by the words.
At small size the visual reads as a pleasant green street, while the data theme remains in the headline rather than an identifiable nonglyph action.

hierarchy.location: right column from upper title to venue, agenda, audience and red registration URLs
hierarchy.observation: The large Korean and English title leads into the event identification and venue. Aligned time rows and horizontal dividers distinguish the programme, audience, registration and contact blocks; red URLs make the action easy to locate.

hierarchy.location: upper-right headline and lower-right red URL pair
hierarchy.observation: The headline remains the dominant textual shape and the red application pair retains a distinct position even when the small body is too reduced for comfortable reading.

typography.location: right column, bilingual title, five agenda rows and footer
typography.observation: Korean glyphs and English words are legible and match the protected copy. The time column stays separate from the descriptions, and wrapped English agenda lines align under the Korean descriptions.

The navy type has clear contrast on cream; paired languages remain legible without collisions. URL punctuation remains readable. The 213-pixel-wide thumbnail makes the long body microscopic, without disrupting the title.

space.location: vertical boundary around x=500 and text rules at approximately x=522–994
space.observation: The illustrated street occupies a substantial continuous left field and the text occupies a consistent right column with aligned starts and ends. Rules create orderly intervals between supporting blocks.

space.location: right edge and bottom organiser pair
space.observation: The column retains a small clear outer margin and bottom clearance; the illustration does not intrude into the supporting copy.

image_material.location: left tree trunk, orange storefront frame, glass and pavement
image_material.observation: Painted foliage, bark, window reflections and paving shadows share a coherent daylight treatment. The simplified blue forms next to the text use visibly flatter treatment but a consistent architectural vocabulary.

image_material.location: left street silhouette and orange doorway
image_material.observation: The main tree and doorway remain distinct, so the large illustration survives reduction as a scene rather than becoming texture.

emotion_control.location: green canopy, orange storefront and navy text on cream
emotion_control.observation: Sunlit greenery and a warm doorway give the event an inviting energy. The restrained, high-contrast information column sustains an institutional tone appropriate to a practical forum.

ai_slop.location: continuous left streetscape and right information column
ai_slop.observation: The scene maintains an intelligible sidewalk perspective, and the supporting rules serve actual information groups. No extra logos, stray words, unlabeled pseudo-statistical marks or unsupported numeric decorations are visible.

The pale outlines have a limited simplification role; no additional decorative motif obscures the copy. The lack of a data relationship is retained under content_form rather than excused by surface polish.

residuals: The information design is resolved, but the large street illustration communicates the city more readily than the city/data relationship. Body copy becomes very small at thumbnail size, while the headline and overall zones remain identifiable.

evidence.observation: M1 uses a continuous painted streetscape on the left and a tall, aligned bilingual information column on the right. This differs structurally from M2’s framed central opening and M3’s joined scene pieces.

M2 uses photographic building/work scenes around a central title and programme, with event logistics at upper left and a two-column footer. Its depth, perimeter collage and text placement differ from both M1 and M3.

M3 gives hands and joined illustrated city pieces a central action, with a top timetable and separate yellow/green lower cards. Unlike M1’s single street and M2’s architectural work scenes, it foregrounds handling and assembling observations.

residuals: All three share leafy contemporary architecture, navy text and warm accents. Their distinct composition, image construction and the third member’s visible action support a strong diversity score of 4, but the set does not reach exceptional thematic breadth. The set score does not cancel M1/M2’s content or mandatory-style failures.
